newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss cancel Marshal Mobutu's visa.
newsitem.headline: Swiss cancel Marshal Mobutu's visa.

text.p: Switzerland has cancelled its visa for Zaire's ailing ruler Mobutu Sese Seko after his departure this month, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Thursday.

Mobutu, who said this week that he intends to return to Lausanne for a medical check-up, left Switzerland on November 4 for the French Riviera where he has a villa. He underwent more than two months of treatment for prostate cancer in Lausanne.

The 66-year-old told French TF-1 television on Monday that he would have a three-day check-up in Switzerland, where he has more than $4 billion in numbered bank accounts according to Swiss media, and then return to his strife-torn country.
But Swiss Foreign Ministry spokesman Jean-Philippe Tissieres said Mobutu's visa had been extended for medical treatment until November 27 as long as he did not leave the country.
"Because of his (Mobutu's) departure, the visa has been automatically cancelled and there is no new visa demand at the moment," he said.
The spokesman declined to say whether a new visa would be granted to Mobutu, who underwent prostate cancer surgery on August 22 in Lausanne's University Hospital.

His presence in Switzerland sparked protests from local deputies in Lausanne who appealed to the federal government to block the dictator's return. Privately, police and other officials breathed a sigh of relief when he packed up.
"After my convalescence here, I'll go back where I was operated so they can do a three-day check-up. Then I'll go home," Mobutu told French television on Monday.

In France, Mobutu has received officials of several governments involved in the creation of an international force to rescue hundreds of thousands of mostly-Rwandan refugees fleeing a Tutsi revolt in eastern Zaire.
In Lausanne, Swiss secrecy and discreet security surrounded the Zairean strongman, whose visitors included France's former Interior Minister Charles Pasqua.
